info.name: Qar API
info.description:
Complete Qar mobile API collection — every registered `api/*` route, each with saved response examples.

**Setup**
1. Import `Qar.postman_environment.json` and select **Qar Production**.
2. `baseUrl` defaults to `https://qar-4uh5.onrender.com`.
3. Register/login requests auto-save `token`. Car/subscription requests auto-save IDs.

**Auth**
- Collection uses Bearer `{{token}}` by default.
- Public endpoints (OTP challenge, packages, QR scan, public menu, Paymob webhook) override with no auth.
- Tokens are mode-scoped: a client token carries `act-as:client`, a merchant token `act-as:merchant`. Use **Account → Switch mode** to swap; it revokes the current token and returns a new one.

**Response examples**
Every example under a request is a real response captured from the app by `tests/Feature/Api/ApiExampleResponsesTest.php`. Regenerate after changing a resource or controller:

```
php artisan test --filter=ApiExampleResponsesTest
php scripts/merge-postman-examples.php
php scripts/check-postman-coverage.php
```

**Worth knowing**
- `user.is_client` / `is_merchant` reflect whether the matching *profile* row exists, not the token mode. A brand-new account has `needs_profile: true` and both flags `false`.
- Google sign-in never returns a phone number, so the response sets `needs_phone: true`; run **OTP → Challenge (link phone)** then **Account → Link OTP (phone)** next.
- `GET /api/menu` returns **201** the first time a merchant calls it, because the menu row is created lazily. Treat 200 and 201 as success.
- `POST /api/print-requests` returns **403** with `"code": "subscription_required"` when the client has no active subscription — branch on that code, not the message.
- File uploads (`POST /api/cars`, `POST /api/menu/items`) are `multipart/form-data`. Menu item updates accept `POST` as well as `PUT` so a multipart body can carry a new image.

item.name: Google
item.description: Google sign-in for the mobile app. The client obtains an ID token from the Google SDK and posts it here; the server verifies it against the client IDs in GOOGLE_CLIENT_IDS.

request.description: Sign-in and sign-up are the same call. A first-time token creates the account (is_new_user = true); a returning token is matched on the Google subject. Google never supplies a phone number, so the response sets needs_phone = true and the app must run the OTP link step next.
